entities.name: Gitanjali
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: Gitanjali is a collection of poems by Rabindranath Tagore, created in the early 20th century. Written in Bengali, these poems are a culmination of Tagore's spiritual and philosophical thoughts, exploring the human condition, love, and the interconnectedness of all things. The poems, which include 'Gitanjali' itself, are a celebration of the universal and the divine, reflecting Tagore's deep understanding of Eastern and Western philosophies. The poems were first published in 1910, and their impact on Indian literature and beyond has been profound, earning Tagore the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. The poems' use of imagery, symbolism, and free verse has influenced generations of writers and artists, making Gitanjali a timeless and universal work of literature.
